scope: G6 fast batch 012: seven image-bearing remaining candidates
write_status: reviewed-only; no production insert authorized until the three approved records are compatibility-aligned and one guarded migration passes full-history isolated PostgreSQL dry-run
review_method: Reviewed seven remaining candidates together to separate migration-ready records from identity, authorship or image blockers.
Opened every local image and rejected images that show the wrong project generation or fail to represent the canonical building.
Checked official project or operator sources for identity, program, dates and design responsibility.
Verified Commons or Flickr creator and open-license metadata for the three approved images.
Queried production read-only: target CASE profiles are absent, required mixed-use and public-space functions and broad types exist, and the only Miyashita name match is the distinct 2020 project.

excluded.reason: Building and CC BY-SA 4.0 image are correct, but no reliable canonical design author has been identified; migration cannot preserve an empty or invented architect.

The current CC BY-SA 4.0 photograph primarily shows the historic hammerhead crane and parking area at night, not the terminal and commercial building; no migration until a representative safe building image is approved.
The current CC BY 3.0 photograph shows the pre-existing roadside station, not Kengo Kuma's 2025 reconstructed project; rights-safe but identity-wrong images are rejected.

The warehouse identity, original Yorinaka Tsumaki authorship and CC BY-SA 3.0 image are verified, but the CASE studies the 2002 cultural-commercial conversion and its canonical renovation design responsibility remains unresolved.

architect_identity.name_zh: Atelier Bow-Wow＋东京工业大学塚本研究室
architect_identity.name_en: Atelier Bow-Wow + Tokyo Institute of Technology Tsukamoto Lab
architect_identity.name_ja: アトリエ・ワン＋東京工業大学塚本研究室

identity_evidence: Atelier Bow-Wow identifies the 2011 Shibuya project as Miyashita Park, designed with Tokyo Institute of Technology Tsukamoto Lab, with a 14,000 square metre park area.
This historical 2011 park is distinct from the 2020 MIYASHITA PARK canonical building already in production.
The image accurately shows the covered sports and circulation space of the 2011 park; Commons identifies Douglas P. Perkins as the own-work creator and licenses it CC BY 3.0.

image.credit: Photo: Douglas P. Perkins / Wikimedia Commons

canonical_building.name_ja: パソナ・アーバンファーム

identity_evidence: Kono Designs identifies Pasona HQ as a nine-storey corporate office renovation integrating offices, auditorium, cafeterias, rooftop garden and urban farming facilities.
Mixed-use is approved as the available function that accurately expresses the deliberate office, food, education and farming combination; the broad building type remains office.
The local image clearly shows the exact Pasona building and planted facade; Commons identifies 螺钉 own work, 3648 by 2736, CC BY-SA 3.0.

architect_identity.name_ja: Hof van Cartesius 協同組合

identity_evidence: The cooperative describes an affordable modular working environment for creative entrepreneurs, self-built from waste and second-hand materials around a regenerative garden.
The official case study explicitly describes a publicly accessible courtyard and social-cultural events, supporting mixed-use primary and public-space secondary while the broad type remains office.
The local image accurately shows the circular material facade and courtyard; the Flickr page identifies nandasluijsmans and CC BY-SA 2.0, with an original 3180 by 2580 image.
